Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

Asian Games Medal Tally after Day 9

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

Article Title: Delhi riots case: High court rejects bail pleas Of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
Article Text:
Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam denied bail by high court

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots.Senior Advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Umar Khalid, submitted that there had been three “small changes in circumstances” since the earlier proceedings. He also referred the court to a Supreme Court judgment in support of his submissions.Pais pointed out that charges have not yet been framed in the case and, consequently, prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The court also noted that the charges were yet to be framed.Pais further submitted that a Special Leave Petition (SLP) is pending before the Supreme Court and that the trial court has indicated it would await the Supreme Court’s order. He then continued his submissions by referring to the Supreme Court judgment.Khalid and Imam had approached the Delhi High Court earlier this year after their bail applications were dismissed by the trial court for the third time on July 4. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.The Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots, PTI reported.The police argued that they could not seek bail on parity with other co-accused, stating that the Supreme Court had earlier categorised them as being part of the “command authority” and held that their “risk profiles” justified “continuing detention”.The police also argued that the present bail pleas were in the teeth of the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which directed them to seek release only after the examination of protected witnesses was completed or after one year, whichever was earlier.On July 4, the trial court rejected Khalid’s bail application, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and could therefore neither entertain the plea nor grant him relief.On September 2, 2025, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to Khalid and Imam. The Supreme Court upheld the verdict on January 5 but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA.On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad, while referring to a larger bench the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA due to the stringent conditions for granting bail.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court refuses to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots. Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots.

Article Title: 'He prayed before attack': Machchhar tells Netanyahu chilling flydubai cockpit ordeal
Article Text:

'There is no pin'

Netanyahu invites Machchhar to Israel

Flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar spoke to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu where he described the incidents that unfolded inside the cockpit. He also described how he managed to open the cockpit door despite suffering repeated blows to his head. Netanyahu praised his courage and said he had "saved so many souls".Machchhar told Netanyahu that the flight had initially been normal. The co-pilot then wanted to play a game that he said many locals play. While Machchhar was looking towards the front of the aircraft, he suddenly felt a heavy blow to the back of his head.Machchhar also told Netanyahu that the co-pilot had wanted to pray before the attack. He said he looked towards the front of the cockpit out of respect while the co-pilot prayed."...while he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back, and suddenly, after, I would say about four-five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head."My first thought was that there was a catastrophic damage to the aircraft and something is not right," Machchhar said.He said the blows continued and he soon realised that the aircraft had not been damaged. Instead, the co-pilot was attacking him."And that's when I realised that it's not the aircraft, it's the other guy who was in the cockpit with me," he said.Machchhar said the initial blows left his vision severely blurred, making it difficult for him to understand what was happening. He then felt the aircraft sharply descending."My memory is still in bits and pieces right now," he told Netanyahu.The pilot also recalled trying to open the cockpit door once, but said the co-pilot shut it again. He later found himself lying on the cockpit floor as he heard the aircraft moving rapidly and passengers screaming.Machchhar said he then realised he had to make one final attempt to reach the door."And as I was telling the ambassador here, that I had that one last fight left in me that, you know, call it personal or call it for people," he said. "But let's say I did it that if I don't do it, I'm going to die."He said he pushed himself towards the door and managed to open it. Crew members and others outside then took control of the situation."And thankfully people were waiting to bounce back, took over the control and the rest is what you know, sir," Machchhar said.Netanyahu asked Machchhar how he had managed to open the cockpit door when the co-pilot was preventing access.Machchhar explained that the door has a twist mechanism on the inside and can normally be opened from outside only using a code. His colleagues outside the cockpit were trying to enter the code, but the attacker was preventing the door from being opened."The only way to open the door was to reach the knob and like any other knob, just to twist it open and it opens on its own," Machchhar said."There is no pin, but yes, the door, it was, it was a short, quick twist, but the point was to reach to that point, to reach to that place."Once he reached the knob, Machchhar said he was able to twist it open.Netanyahu repeatedly praised Machchhar during the conversation, calling him a hero of India, Israel and the world."I, frankly, I'm amazed at your courage, at your coolness of judgement under impossible conditions," Netanyahu said.He said Machchhar's actions had helped save lives and described the incident as an example of how courage could overcome violence."You're a hero of Israel. You're a hero of India. You're a hero of the entire world," Netanyahu said.The Israeli prime minister also said Machchhar would be welcomed in Israel and invited him and his family to visit.Netanyahu said he wanted Machchhar and PM Modi to light a celebratory flame at Israel's next Independence Day ceremony. He described the honour as one usually reserved for Israeli citizens."I really would like them to bear a celebratory flame. It's our highest honour that we give in our Independence Day. It's usually reserved for Israeli citizens," Netanyahu said."But I think here in this case, all the citizens of Israel will, will embrace you. They do now and they will then too."Machchhar thanked Netanyahu and said he looked forward to meeting him in Israel.Netanyahu ended the conversation by wishing the pilot a speedy recovery and saying his visit to Israel would be "memorable and historic".
Article Summary: Flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar spoke to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He described the incidents that unfolded inside the cockpit. He also described how he managed to open the cockpit door despite suffering repeated blows to his head. Netanyahu praised his courage and said he had "saved so many souls"

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday said the focus of the alliance should be on ensuring victory rather than negotiating the number of seats each party gets, amid discussions over seat-sharing.In a post on X, Yadav reiterated that the alliance should remain united and work towards a collective victory, while seeking to dismiss any differences over seat allocation."When the goal is clear, hand in hand we stand. When the gaze is fixed on the destination, the journey becomes easy! The big thing isn't how many seats the alliance gets or which seat goes to whom—the big thing is that we all must ensure that the victory belongs to the alliance.""Let us repeat again: It's not about the seats, it's about the victory.This victory will be greater than the parties in our alliance—it will be the victory of all of us, of that united effort that persists in struggle so that communalism may never raise its head again, so that BJP's influence may not touch democracy, the Constitution, or reservations, and so that the country's harmony may bloom once more, and the nation's progress and prosperity may smile again.Victory to the Constitution—Victory to Hindustan!" he added.Earlier on Saturday Yadav directed party leaders to keep their views on seat-sharing negotiations and the Congress within internal party channels, as differences over the alliance surfaced ahead of formal talks for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.The intervention came after public remarks by SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel, with Yadav seeking to ease the growing friction between the two INDIA bloc allies.Addressing reporters at an event in Lucknow, Yadav urged party leaders to refrain from airing their views publicly on the alliance and seat-sharing discussions.Uttar Pradesh is set to go to the polls in 2027, with the BJP and the Samajwadi Party expected to be the principal contenders.In the 2022 Assembly elections, the BJP retained power by winning 255 of the state’s 403 seats, securing a vote share of 41.29%.The Akhilesh Yadav-led Samajwadi Party finished second with 111 seats and 32.06% of the votes.The Bahujan Samaj Party and the Congress were reduced to single-digit tallies, winning one and two seats, respectively. The BSP secured 12.88% of the vote, while the Congress recorded a vote share of 2.33%.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav says focus of alliance should be on ensuring victory. Yadav reiterates that alliance should remain united and work towards a collective victory. Article Title: Congress resets Team Uttar Pradesh: 5 clear messages for BJP and Akhilesh Yadav
Article Text:
Congress replaced Ajay Rai with Aradhana Misra Mona as Uttar Pradesh Congress chief.

1. A bigger, but amicable, say at seat-sharing table

What Mona Misra said after her appointment as UP Congress chief

2. Rebuilding old social reach, but with a new mix

What Ajay Rai said after being replaced as UP Congress chief

3. Not conceding Muslim vote

What Imran Masood said after UP Congress organizational reshuffle

4. Congress wants credibility

5. Women power at heart

NEW DELHI: Congress has overhauled its Uttar Pradesh organisation ahead of the 2027 assembly election, replacing Ajay Rai with three-time Rampur Khas MLA Aradhana Misra Mona as state unit president and appointing Saharanpur MP Imran Masood as working president. The party has also named Chaudhary Virendra Singh as Congress legislature party leader.The reshuffle brings together a prominent Brahmin leader from eastern UP, a Muslim leader with influence in western UP, and Dalit and OBC representation in senior organisational positions. Rajendra Pal Gautam, a Dalit leader, is already the party's Uttar Pradesh in-charge. With these recent appointments, Congress may be trying to widen its social and regional reach after years of electoral decline in the state.Taken together, the appointments suggest that Congress is trying to do two things at once: strengthen its bargaining position with the Samajwadi Party while rebuilding an independent political identity in Uttar Pradesh.The timing is important. The 2024 Lok Sabha election revived Congress's presence in UP through its alliance with Akhilesh Yadav . But Akhilesh’s party remains the much larger organisation in the state. In the 2024 polls, SP moved 32 seats up and won 37 seats, registering a 15.73% gain in vote share.On the other hand, Congress also slightly improved its Lok Sabha tally with 6 seats and a jump of a little over 3% vote share.Congress is now trying to turn that electoral revival into a more substantial organisational base before the 2027 assembly election in a state which has been long associated with Congress's political success story.Here are the five messages embedded in the reset.The appointment of Aradhana Misra Mona as UPCC president, along with the elevation of Imran Masood, suggests that Congress wants to push for a larger share of assembly seats while keeping its relationship with the Samajwadi Party workable.Masood has been unusually vocal about Congress' seat demand. On September 3, he argued that if Congress' electoral performance continued to improve, its share of seats should also increase."Hum koi bhikhari hain jo Samajwadi Party se bheekh mangenge? ... Party formula tay karegi, lekin jo formula Lok Sabha election mein tha, woh formula nahi hoga. (Are we beggars who will beg from Samajwadi Party? ... The party will decide the formula, but it will not be the same formula used in the Lok Sabha elections)," he had told ANI.Congress' UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam has also spoken of seeking an equal number of seats with the SP, while Masood has backed a 50:50 formula.The rhetoric sharpened on September 28, when Masood directly declared: "If Akhilesh Yadav is unhappy (with seat-sharing discussion), the loss will be his own... We fail to understand what the anger is even about."Mona's elevation, on the other hand, sends a somewhat different signal. Unlike the more combative rhetoric around seat-sharing, her appointment gives Congress a state president who is seen as having a more workable equation with the SP leadership. Her political experience and close association with the Congress leadership also give her a role in managing the alliance even as the party pushes for greater space.The numbers give Congress some basis for making that argument. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the SP won 37 of UP's 80 seats while Congress won six, taking the INDIA bloc's combined tally to 43. The SP's 37-seat tally was a dramatic rise from five seats in 2019.However, going by the numbers, Congress cannot negotiate from the position of higher power and will most likely have to settle for the junior partner role.But how "small" the partner role it gets will be crucial.One of the clearest messages in the new team is social and regional balancing.Mona is a prominent Brahmin face from eastern Uttar Pradesh. Masood brings a prominent Muslim face from western UP. Devinder Nishad gives the organisation an OBC, riverine-community face, while Alok Prasad brings Dalit representation into the senior state team. Rajendra Pal Gautam is already the party's Dalit in-charge for Uttar Pradesh.The choice of Mona is particularly significant because she replaces Ajay Rai, a Bhumihar leader, with another upper-caste leader from a different community. The switch from Rai to Mona could be read as an attempt to reconnect with Brahmin voters who were traditionally associated with Congress but have, over time, moved substantially towards the BJP.This rejig comes at a time when the upper-caste groups (Rajputs, Brahmins, Tyagis) reportedly feel increasingly sidelined by BJP's aggressive outreach toward non-Yadav OBC and Dalit vote banks. Tensions stem from ticket distribution cuts, perceived administrative favour toward Rajputs over Brahmins, and farmers' issues.Mona's appointment, however, is not simply a return to Congress's old social formula. The new team combines upper-caste, Muslim, Dalit and OBC representation, while also distributing the leadership geographically between eastern and western UP.The BJP has built a broad social coalition of its own in Uttar Pradesh. Congress' organisational response now appears to be an attempt to create multiple social entry points into the party rather than rely on a single caste or community bloc.Masood's elevation carries another particularly important message for western Uttar Pradesh.The Saharanpur MP is one of Congress' most prominent Muslim leaders in the state, and his appointment puts a western UP Muslim face in the second-most important position in the state organisation. His appointment seems to be a direct attempt to attract and consolidate Muslim support.That matters because the SP has traditionally been the principal opposition party competing for the Muslim vote in UP. The 2024 Lok Sabha election demonstrated the strength of that relationship.A post-election CSDS-Lokniti analysis estimated that 77% of Muslim respondents in Uttar Pradesh voted for the SP and 15% for Congress, while 2% reported voting for the BJP. These are, of course, survey estimates and not absolute vote counts. However, it may reflect the trend.The actual election results also showed the importance of Muslim-heavy constituencies to the opposition's performance. Congress won Saharanpur and Sitapur, while the SP and its allies captured several other such seats.Masood's promotion therefore gives Congress a prominent vehicle to seek Muslim support directly rather than relying entirely on the SP to bring that constituency into the alliance.Mona's appointment is significant because she brings an electoral record to the top of the state unit.She first entered the Uttar Pradesh assembly through a bypoll in 2014 and subsequently retained Rampur Khas in the 2017 and 2022 elections. She has therefore won the seat three times. Before entering the assembly, she served as block pramukh of Sangramgarh from 2002 to 2014 and held positions in the organisation and cooperative sector.Her 2022 victory was particularly notable because Congress was reduced to just two assembly seats across Uttar Pradesh. She defeated BJP's Nagesh Pratap Singh by 14,741 votes, polling 84,334 votes, or 50.27%, according to Election Commission data.That gives Congress a state president who is not merely an organisational appointee but an incumbent with a repeated assembly-winning record.The appointment of Aradhana Misra Mona also gives Congress a prominent woman at the helm of its Uttar Pradesh organisation, at a time when BJP too is putting renewed emphasis on its women leaders in the state.The timing is notable. The BJP has recently brought back Smriti Irani into a more prominent organisational role, signalling that women leaders continue to have an important place in its political strategy. Irani, who beat Rahul Gandhi and represented Amethi in the Lok Sabha from 2019 to 2024, remains one of the BJP's most recognisable women faces in Uttar Pradesh.The Mona-Priyanka Gandhi combination will give Congress a big women power picture it can easily put on its posters.The wider electoral numbers also underline why women matter. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the Election Commission recorded female voter turnout in Uttar Pradesh at 57.22%, compared with 56.46% among men. Women therefore turned out at a slightly higher rate than men in the state.As a bonus, Mona's elevation also gives Congress a combination of representation and political substance: a woman leader, a Brahmin face, a three-time assembly winner and someone with an established organisational network.The new UP team combines experience with caste, community, regional and gender representation, giving Congress multiple entry points in the voter base. The real test now will be whether the reshuffle can translate into stronger grassroots organisation and enough bargaining power ahead of the 2027 assembly election.
Article Summary: Congress replaced Ajay Rai with Aradhana Misra Mona as Uttar Pradesh Congress chief. The party has also named Chaudhary Virendra Singh as Congress legislature party leader. The reshuffle brings together a prominent Brahmin leader from eastern UP, a Muslim leader with influence in western UP.

Article Title: ‘He was so scared’: SP MP on ally Rahul Gandhi skipping Amethi in 2024 Lok Sabha polls
Article Text:
"Rahul Gandhi was reluctant to contest the 2024 Lok Sabha election from Amethi," says Congress ally.

Patel credits SP for Congress wins

SP MP dismisses Congress's caste strategy

Congress hits back

NEW DELHI: Strain deepened within the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance ahead of Uttar Pradesh polls, with SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel in an off-the-cuff remark claimed that Rahul Gandhi was "reluctant to contest the 2024 Lok Sabha election" from Amethi and chose Raebareli because he was "so scared".Patel, who represents Pratapgarh, also credited the SP-Congress alliance for the Congress's six Lok Sabha wins in Uttar Pradesh, arguing that the party would have drawn a blank in the state without SP's support.Speaking to news agency PTI, Patel said the SP leadership had to persuade Gandhi to contest from Raebareli after he appeared unwilling to fight from Amethi, the traditional Gandhi family constituency."Had there been no alliance (with the Samajwadi Party ), they (Congress) wouldn't have won a single seat. It even reached a point where their top leader Rahul Gandhi was ready to give up his seat. He contested from elsewhere (Raebareli) instead of Amethi. He was so scared," he said.The leader futher added: "It was our national president who reassured and persuaded him, asking him to contest and warning that if he didn't, he (Akhilesh) would field his own candidate. Only then did Gandhi agree to contest. Otherwise, he was extremely reluctant to run for that traditional seat, the one said to belong to the Nehru family.Gandhi only managed to win it because of that persuasion," he said.Patel said SP voters backed Congress candidates in constituencies allotted to the Congress under the alliance arrangement."Every single vote from the Samajwadi Party went to the Congress wherever they were allotted seats. That is precisely how they managed to win those six seats," he said.The SP won 37 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 elections, while Congress won six. The BJP won 33 seats, while the NDA's tally in the state stood at 36.Patel said the difference in the two parties' performances should be reflected in any future seat-sharing discussions."We secured 37 seats. We are far ahead of the Congress in every respect. They shouldn't ask for more than 50, and should feel happy. The Congress should cooperate, rather than making all sorts of absurd or negative remarks," Patel said.Patel also criticised the Congress's reported caste strategy in Uttar Pradesh, including its appointment of a Brahmin as state Congress president and a Muslim as working president."This will not yield any benefit. Look, Dalits were with Mayawati, but they have now shifted to our side. They realised that there was no significant upliftment of Dalits during the Congress regime, and certainly none is happening under the BJP. Whereas, during the Samajwadi Party's tenure, everyone gets equal opportunities. Everyone gets an equal chance to progress; their children get a chance to receive an education. "He added, "That is precisely why the party was named 'Samajwadi'. Our party operates based on the ideals of (Ram Manohar) Lohia-ji. Our party's objective is the welfare of all sections of society."The SP currently has 101 MLAs in the 403-member Uttar Pradesh Assembly, while Congress has two.Patel said the SP could benefit from continuing its alliance with Congress, but argued that the Congress would suffer more if it contested elections without its regional ally."If we proceed with an alliance, we will certainly benefit. Even if it doesn't happen, we won't have any significant loss. But for them, the tally will drop to zero. I can say this with confidence: if they don't contest as part of an alliance, they will end up with zero seats.The public will realise they are fielding candidates solely to split votes. If they act as vote-spoilers, they will be reduced to zero," Patel said.Uttar Pradesh Congress spokesperson Anshu Awasthi pushed back against Patel's remarks and said the SP should rein in leaders making such statements."The Samajwadi Party must work to rein in leaders who make such statements. It is because of the INDIA bloc that he (Patel) has become an MP. He should know his limits and avoid making statements like these," Awasthi told PTI.
Article Summary: SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel claims Rahul Gandhi was "reluctant to contest the 2024 Lok Sabha election" from Amethi. Article Title: 'No time to experiment': Captain Shubman Gill wants all resources available for India's ODI World Cup prep
Article Text:
India's Rohit Sharma and skipper Shubman Gill (ANI Photo)

Kamboj, Nabi on trial for No. 8 spot

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Fielding woes

New Chandigarh: If one takes a quick scan of India’s ODI resources for next year’s World Cup in South Africa, the pace cupboard wears a bare and fragile look. There’s only Jasprit Bumrah who truly commands a place in the XI. The rest are either on trial or nursing injuries. Mohammed Siraj has gone off the boil dramatically, losing the confidence of the team management. The other ‘experienced’ pacer in the ranks, Prasidh Krishna, was still in the process of establishing his credentials before breaking down in the second ODI. TOI understands that the team management has identified Gurnoor Brar as a strong prospect in South African conditions.It’s been a rough initiation into ODI captaincy for Shubman Gill . It’s been a year since he assumed the role, but he is yet to get all of his first-choice resources at his disposal. “It’s been unfortunate with the injuries and with the scheduling. We have not been able to play the bowling line-up that we would like to. It’s a great chance for them to showcase their skills,” Gill said after the series win over West Indies here on Saturday.The anxiety was apparent, though. He declared the need for urgency in sorting out the ODI core. With Bumrah away playing in the Asian Games, this series was meant to check the second line of pacers.But Gill doesn’t seem to be in any mood to be in the experimental phase. “I honestly think there is not that much time to experiment. The combination that we want to play, hopefully we get all the players that are available from the next series. The combination that we would like to play in the World Cup, we want to start playing with that combination,” he stated.Here’s the catch. The next series is a five-ODI affair in New Zealand, which will be followed by a two-Test series. Precariously placed in the World Test Championship table, the team management intends to pull out the Test regulars after the third ODI. That would mean Bumrah, Krishna and Siraj will not be available for the entire series. There’s a strong chance Brar, too, could be pulled out.Pace bowling was India’s biggest asset in the last two World Cups. Bumrah, Mohammed Shami, Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Mohammed Siraj were incisive with the new ball and potent in the death overs. Gill clearly sees the gap in his bowling attack.“Bowling in the power play and in the death have hurt us. If you don’t get off to a good start in the power play, it’s not easy to take wickets in the middle overs. It’s not easy to create chances with only four fielders outside the ring. The intensity of the game is completely different if you don’t keep taking wickets either in the power play or in the middle overs. That’s why this series has been so high scoring. Even today we lost two wickets in the power play but we still managed to get 350 on the board,” Gill spelt out his concerns.It’s not just about the new-ball bowlers. Gill also revealed that the team management is looking for a pacer who can be a capable batter at No. 8. Recurring injuries to Harshit Rana have compounded Gill’s problems. Which is why Auqib Nabi and Anshul Kamboj were handed debuts in this series.“Anshul and Auqib are going to be in the mix a lot. Anshul is someone who can also bat at No. 8. And that number is very crucial for us. We don’t know who will be fit at the World Cup. And if we want someone who can bowl and can bat a bit at No. 8, Anshul can do the job. And even Aqib can bat a bit and do the job. So, we want to see which players can deliver under pressure,” Gill said.Both Kamboj and Nabi endured rough debuts, conceding runs at over nine runs per over. However, this is the only spot where Gill may be willing to bide his time.“They would have liked to have done a much better job. But you know, a little bit harsh on them. It’s not easy to come and to be able to deliver straight away. I hope that they learn from their mistakes and the opportunities that they get,” Gill said.Gill also made his displeasure about the fielding standards of the team clear. The Indian team’s fielding has worsened over the last eight months.“We dropped around three or four catches today. I don’t think Shai was dropped but still dropping three or four catches breaks the momentum of the team. Our fielding in the series, I would say, has not been up to the mark. I think in the whole series we dropped around seven catches, if I am not wrong. And even in the field today we gave away, many times in the field we were quite sloppy,” he said.“I think leading up to the World Cup, these are the areas where we definitely need to get better at. We need to be at the peak of our powers, especially when we are in the field. It’s not easy for the bowlers, so the fielders can help a lot. And if the wicket is not helping much for the bowlers and the fielding being substandard, it’s a difficult job for the bowlers,” he added.
Article Summary: Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Shami, Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Mohammed Siraj were incisive with the new ball and potent in the death overs. Gill also revealed that the team management is looking for a pacer who can be a capable batter at No. 8. Recurring injuries to Harshit Rana have compounded Gill’s problems.

Article Title: EXCLUSIVE | Asian Games gold done, Neeru Dhanda eyes Olympic shotgun medal to end wait since Rajyavardhan Rathore’s 2004 silver
Article Text:
India's Neeru Dhanda (PTI Photo)

From illness to three medals

Nagoya: From left, India's Manisha Keer, Ashima Ahlawat and Neeru Dhanda pose with the national flag after winning the silver medal. (PTI Photo)

Mission Olympics begins

‘Golden girl’? Neeru loves it

Little time with family

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Days before leaving for the Asian Games 2026, Neeru Dhanda was hospitalised with viral fever. She had barely any time to recover before boarding the flight to Japan. There was no proper recovery period. Just medicines, ORS, and a dream of winning a medal at the Asian Games.When she reached Aichi-Nagoya and entered her hotel room, Neeru picked up her gun and told herself three words: "Nerru, tu training pe hai (Neeru, you are in training."It was a message she wanted to give her own mind - a way of staying focused and refusing to think about the illness.With water bottles, ORS and medicines by her side, Neeru kept her dream alive. The trap shooter, who had won gold at the ISSF World Cup in Lonato earlier this year, eventually stepped onto the range, loaded her ammunition and shot her way to glory.She finished the Asian Games with three medals - two golds and a silver - emerging as one of India's standout performers.Neeru first won gold in the women's individual trap event. She then teamed up with Manisha Keer and Aashima Ahlawat to win silver in the women's trap team event.On the penultimate day of the shooting competition, she partnered Kynan Chenai to win gold in the trap mixed team event.But behind the three medals was a battle that began even before she reached the shooting range.“I didn't let my mind receive the message that I was sick or unwell. I didn't want to let myself think that I was sick. Whenever I felt down or weak, I used to tell myself loudly, ‘Neeru, tu training pe hai abhi.’ This is what kept me motivated throughout the Asian Games,” Neeru told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview.“Honestly, I felt very weak because there was no recovery period after the hospitalisation. I thought about skipping the Games, but no, I am very stubborn. I wanted to do something different. Very few people get this opportunity. I was lucky that I got it, and I am happy that I delivered,” she said.Neeru dedicated her three-medal haul to late Raja Randhir Singh, India's first Asian Games shooting gold medallist, who passed away aged 79 in May. Randhir, a five-time Olympian, had won India's first Asian Games shooting gold in 1978.Neeru had met him a few times and remembered the encouragement he gave her.“I dedicate these medals to late Raja Randhir Singh. He was a lovely soul. I got to meet him a couple of times. Whenever he met me, he blessed me. He always said, ‘Beta, be brave. You are a shooter, you need to be brave. Shoot with bravery, you will get the result.’ Those words helped me a lot in Aichi-Nagoya,” Neeru said."I also want to dedicate to my federation, SAI, SAI Bhopal, Bhopa Shooting Academy where I train, my coaches, and everyone who has been with me throughout this journey," she said.The World Cup is done. The Asian Games are done. Now, Neeru has set her sights on the Los Angeles Olympics. Her immediate target is the World Championship in Doha, which will offer a quota opportunity for the 2028 Olympics.“The moment I leave Japan, my target will shift towards the World Championship in Doha. That is a quota competition for the Los Angeles Olympics, so I will focus on that. That is my ultimate goal. Olympics mein medal jeetna hai,” she said.India have won several Olympic medals in shooting, but the shotgun disciplines have produced only one Olympic medal for the country - Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore's silver in men's double trap at the 2004 Athens Olympics.After her performances in Aichi-Nagoya, Neeru will be one of the Indian shooters attracting attention ahead of the Los Angeles Games.Neeru has also earned the nickname ‘golden girl’ after her recent run of success. Asked about the title, she laughed.“Golden girl title... I just love it. I love this title. I hope it continues to be like this always. It was possible because of the hard work I have put in day and night,” she said.For Neeru, the key has been constantly looking back at her own performances and learning from her mistakes.“Introspection has always helped me. Whenever I do something wrong or make mistakes, I ask myself, ‘Where did I go wrong?’ I get that answer. That helps me a lot,” she said.After returning home with three medals, Neeru was eager to meet her parents and family and celebrate her success with them.But she had only a few hours. Neeru was at her home in Sangatpura village in Jind, speaking to her mother, when she received a call that gave her another reason to return to Japan.Former India shooter and deputy chef de mission Anjali Bhagwat told her that she had been selected as India's women's flag bearer for the closing ceremony of the Asian Games 2026. Within hours, Neeru packed her bags and headed back to the airport.“I got a call from Anjali Bhagwat ma'am. She asked me to be the flag bearer at the closing ceremony. It's a big honour for me. I didn't want to let it go,” Neeru told TimesofIndia.com.Her parents were delighted by the news. “My parents are so happy. When I gave them the news about the closing ceremony, my mother said, ‘Ja beta, mauka nahi milta ye kisi ko. Aaja, phir se khushi manayenge,’” Neeru said.
Article Summary: Neeru Dhanda won three medals at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. She dedicated her three-medal haul to late Raja Randhir Singh, India's first Asian Games shooting gold medallist, who passed away in May. Neeru has set her sights on the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.

Gracie Hunt is marking the start of another Kansas City Chiefs season with a charity milestone that goes far beyond football. Ahead of the Chiefs’ September 14 clash with the Denver Broncos, Hunt highlighted a longstanding Kansas City tradition that has raised more than $7.5 million for Ronald McDonald House Kansas City. The fundraising campaign, built around limited-edition Chiefs flags, has connected fans with families facing difficult medical circumstances for more than a decade. For Hunt, the milestone also reflects a family tradition of community service that has shaped her approach to life and her role around the Chiefs.Hunt shared the update on Instagram while preparing for the new NFL season. The campaign gives Chiefs fans a simple way to support families who travel to Kansas City while their children receive medical care.“In celebration of the start of a new season, this longstanding tradition brings the Kansas City community together to give back to families in need. Over the past 13 years, sales of limited-edition flags have raised more than $7.5 million for Ronald McDonald House Kansas City.”The commemorative flags have traditionally been sold at participating McDonald’s restaurants and Hy-Vee stores, with contributions starting at $5 in some locations.Online versions have also been available.The money supports Ronald McDonald House Kansas City, which provides temporary accommodation for families with children receiving treatment at nearby hospitals. That support can make a major difference for parents who need to stay close to their children during long and stressful hospital stays.The 2025 campaign reportedly raised $1 million on its own, showing how the annual tradition has grown into a significant community fundraiser.The charity effort also fits with the values Hunt has previously described as central to her upbringing. In an interview with Interview Magazine, she credited her parents with teaching her to look beyond her own circumstances and understand the importance of helping others.“I’m so thankful that my parents raised me the way they did with a humble outlook on life.”She also explained how seeing different parts of the world shaped her perspective.“And also to have been to what the world looks like beyond how I grew up, and beyond what the United States at large looks like.”Hunt added that her family encouraged her to make service part of her life.“They really impressed upon us the importance of service, of giving back and of being involved, in really leaving your legacy as one that leaves the world a better place. And that’s where my passion for service in the Special Olympics began.”With the $7.5 million milestone now reached, the Chiefs’ annual flag tradition remains a visible example of how football fandom can translate into support for Kansas City families.

Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti praised India’s effort and defensive organisation despite Brazil beating the hosts 4-0 in an international friendly in Kolkata on Saturday, October 3. He said India stayed organised, defended well and looked to attack on the counter, making the game a useful test for both sides.India managed to stay competitive for the first 25 minutes before Brazil gradually took control of the match. The visitors also had 20 shots, with seven on target, while India managed nine attempts and three on target.Brazil had 29 attacking touches inside India’s penalty area compared to India’s 12. Their passing was also much more effective, with 90.3% accuracy from 652 passes, while India completed 83.6% of their 330 passes.India made 23 clearances and six tackles, showing the amount of defensive work they had to do. Amethyst Lens - Howling Woods

It is found in the Howling Woods, which is the second Overworld area unlocked in the game. From the Hidden Grove fast travel minecart station, head down past the waterfall, then climb the hilly area to reach a platforming section. Jump across the platforms to a higher level, then turn left into a hidden area containing the chest. Equipping it boosts ranged attack damage.

Emerald of Good Fortune - Lullaby Hills

Reach the Lullaby Hilltop checkpoint in the Sift dimension, head right, then continue straight to a series of bridges on the left. Carefully cross them to the bottom, where a group of Illagers will ambush you. Clear them out and open the secret chest to claim it.

Glowstone Flask - Overworld Dungeons

This one uses a random acquisition method. It spawns in any Overworld dungeon that generates with a four-brazier layout. Keep clearing dungeons until that layout appears, then extinguish all four lit braziers to reveal the hidden chest. It significantly speeds up potion cooldowns.

Lucky Clover - Frozen Highlands

Head to the Frozen Fortress checkpoint and make your way to the Library Towers. Climb the stairs to a bridge with a broken railing at its center, then jump down and head left to find a small catapult. It launches you onto an elevated platform containing the secret chest. This Talisman grants a 2% chance at bonus loot drops from defeated enemies.

Justine Pissott has spoken publicly about surviving sexual assault, explaining why the continuing attention around the Cornell 7 case has been especially difficult for her. The Las Vegas Aces guard shared the deeply personal message on Instagram as public discussion intensified around allegations involving seven former Cornell University fraternity members. Rather than focusing only on the allegations, Pissott used her platform to highlight the lasting impact trauma can have on survivors and the importance of offering compassion instead of questioning how they respond.Pissott, 22, said the Cornell case brought back emotions connected to her own experience. In a message shared on September 29, she explained that she had rarely spoken about what happened to her but felt compelled to do so after seeing the public reaction to the case.“This is a vulnerable message but something I want to share,” Pissott began. “As someone who has been drugged and rap--, the Cornell 7 situation has been really hard for me to see. It hits a place in me that I don’t talk about often.”She went on to describe how the effects of sexual assault can continue long after the incident itself.“When something like this happens to you, it doesn’t just end when that night ends. You carry it with you.The confusion, the pieces you can’t remember, questioning yourself, blaming yourself, and trying to understand how someone could take advantage of you when you weren’t even able to protect yourself.”Pissott also addressed the scrutiny survivors can face when they choose to speak about their experiences.The basketball player said people often ask why survivors waited to speak, remained silent or behaved differently afterwards. She argued that trauma does not follow one predictable pattern.She also expressed support for the woman at the centre of the Cornell case and said survivors should not feel pressured to respond in a particular way.Pissott said she was not sharing her story to receive sympathy. Instead, she wanted other survivors to know they were not alone.“And if sharing even a small part of my story makes another survivor feel less alone, then it’s worth it,” Pissott wrote.She ended by offering encouragement to survivors and calling for an environment where people can speak about sexual assault without being judged for how they coped with the experience.The Cornell case involves a civil complaint filed by a former student against Cornell University and seven Chi Phi fraternity members. The allegations remain allegations, and the defendants’ legal responses are part of the ongoing proceedings.

Article Title: Tennessee prison chief Frank Strada resigns after Christa Pike's botched execution; governor orders review
Article Text:
Strada said his resignation was 'in the best interest of Tennesseans' while the review is conducted and defended the state's execution process

Problems with IV lines blamed

Second failed execution since May

Strada's record in Tennessee and Arizona

Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada will resign this month following the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike, Governor Bill Lee announced Saturday, as the state faces growing calls for answers over the second botched execution attempt in five months.Lee also appointed former US Attorney Ed Stanton to lead an independent review of what went wrong during Pike's execution attempt on Wednesday. The governor has halted further executions while the review is under way.Strada said his resignation was “in the best interest of Tennesseans” while the review is conducted. He defended the state's execution process, saying he believed Tennessee “carried out its responsibilities in accordance with the established protocol.”Pike, 50, remained unconscious and on a ventilator in hospital after the state administered two doses of the lethal drug pentobarbital but failed to complete her execution. Her lawyers said hospital staff were trying to clear the drug from her system. There was no immediate update on her condition from her legal team on Saturday.Pike's lawyers welcomed Strada's departure but said it “does nothing to help Christa now.”“What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person,” the four-lawyer team said. “We hope the governor’s call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee’s entire death penalty system.”The execution attempt has drawn criticism from both supporters and opponents of the death penalty. Pike's lawyers said they believed problems with the IV lines caused the pentobarbital to enter her body rather than her bloodstream.Pike was reportedly cooperative as the execution team struggled to insert the IV lines. Her lawyer Randy Spivey said she even told staff, “please try here, please try here” as they attempted to place the lines.The incident was the second time since May that Tennessee stopped an execution after a prisoner appeared to be close to death. In May, officials halted the execution of Tony Carruthers after they managed to place an IV in his right arm but could not establish a second line. Lee later ordered that Carruthers not be executed again for at least a year.Stanton has previously reviewed problems with Tennessee's lethal injection process. In 2022, Lee appointed him to examine why another execution was called off. Stanton concluded that the state had failed to follow its own lethal injection procedures.Strada became commissioner of Tennessee's Department of Correction in January 2023 after serving as deputy director of the Arizona Department of Corrections. In late 2024, he announced that Tennessee would change its lethal injection protocol and use only pentobarbital.His record in Arizona has also come under scrutiny. Court filings show that Strada oversaw executions there when the state resumed carrying them out in 2022 after an eight-year pause.During the execution of Clarence Dixon that year, medical staff struggled to find a vein and eventually made an incision in his groin to administer the drugs. The process lasted about 25 minutes.Medical staff also initially struggled to find a vein during Frank Atwood's execution in 2022 before inserting an IV into his right hand. During Murray Hooper's execution later that year, an attempt to place an IV in his right arm failed, while a line inserted in his leg entered his femoral artery.“When Governor Lee hired Strada to fix execution problems in Tennessee, his problematic history of executions in Arizona was well known,” said Kit Thomas, an attorney who has represented people on Tennessee's death row.
Article Summary: Christa Pike, 50, remained unconscious and on a ventilator in hospital after the state administered two doses of the lethal drug pentobarbital but failed to complete her execution. Governor Bill Lee has appointed former US Attorney Ed Stanton to lead an independent review of what went wrong during Pike's execution attempt on Wednesday. Strada said his resignation was 'in the best interest of Tennesseans' while the review is conducted.

India fall short of Hangzhou record but finish strongly

India signed off from the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya with a strong fourth-place finish, winning 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.While India fell short of its record-breaking 106-medal haul at the Hangzhou Asian Games, the Aichi-Nagoya campaign was marked by a late surge, several historic firsts and dominant performances in sports such as athletics, shooting, archery, boxing and team events.Around 500 Indian athletes competed at the continental multi-sport event, with the country eventually finishing among the top five in the medal standings.Here is the complete sport-wise medal tally for India at the Asian Games 2026:Archery led the gold-medal standings with five golds. Shooting and boxing followed with three gold medals each, while wrestling contributed two.India also won two gold medals apiece in cricket, hockey and kabaddi, with both men's and women's teams contributing to the country's strong finish.India's medals came across 21 sports, demonstrating the breadth of its performance at the continental event.Alongside the major medal-winning disciplines, India also secured podium finishes in weightlifting, wushu, badminton, kurash, mixed martial arts, rowing, sepaktakraw, soft tennis and table tennis.The 85-medal haul was India's second-highest ever at the Asian Games, behind the record 106 medals won at Hangzhou 2023.India's final tally of 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals secured the country a fourth-place finish in the overall medal standings.Athletics was the backbone of India's medal campaign, producing a wide range of podium finishes across track and field events.India won gold in the women's 4x400m relay, while athletes also collected medals in the 10,000m, 1500m, marathon, shot put, long jump, high jump, javelin throw, pole vault, 400m hurdles, 5000m, 3000m steeplechase, 200m, decathlon and relay events.Gulveer Singh was among India's standout performers, winning silver in the men's 10,000m and 1500m events and bronze in the 5000m.Sawan Berwal won silver in the men's marathon, becoming India's first marathon medallist at the Asian Games since 1982 while also setting a national record.Sarvesh Kushare ended India's 56-year wait for a men's high jump medal, while Baranica Elangovan created history by becoming the first Indian pole vaulter to win an Asian Games medal.Vithya Ramraj added another landmark performance by winning bronze in the women's 400m hurdles and breaking a national record that had stood for 42 years.Shooting once again played a major role in India's Asian Games campaign, contributing 15 medals, including three golds.Neeru Dhanda won India's first individual gold medal of the Games in the women's trap competition. She later combined with Kynan Chenai to win gold in the mixed trap event.Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh also won gold in the mixed team 10m air pistol event, matching the Asian record.India's shooters also collected medals in the 10m air rifle, 50m rifle 3P, 25m pistol, trap and skeet events.Archery was India's most successful sport in terms of gold medals, with five titles.Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Prithika Pradeep and Chikitha Taniparthi won gold in the women's compound team event, while Chikitha Taniparthi and Sahil Jadhav claimed the mixed compound team title.Sahil Jadhav, Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru and Kushal Dalal won the men's compound team gold.The women's recurve team of Ankita Bhakat, Kumkum Mohod and Kirti Sharma also finished on top.Kumkum then produced one of the defining moments of the Games by winning India's first-ever women's individual recurve gold medal at the Asian Games.India enjoyed a strong showing in boxing, winning three gold medals.Lovlina Borgohain became only the second Indian woman to win an Asian Games boxing gold, following Mary Kom's historic achievement at the 2014 Incheon Games.Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal also won gold medals in their respective categories.India added bronze medals through Narender Berwal, Priya Ghanghas and Kapil Pokhariya.India's wrestlers also made their mark in Aichi-Nagoya.Aman Sehrawat won gold in the men's 57kg category, while Sujeet Kalkal became champion in the men's 65kg event.Nitesh Kumar and Antim Panghal won silver medals, while Sunil Kumar and Deepak Punia added bronze medals.India's team sports produced a spectacular late surge.The men's and women's cricket teams successfully defended their Asian Games titles. The men's team defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the final, while the women's team beat Sri Lanka to retain the gold medal.Hockey also delivered two gold medals.The Indian women's hockey team ended a 44-year wait for an Asian Games title, while the men's team, led by Harmanpreet Singh, completed its campaign with a commanding 5-1 victory over Malaysia in the final.The men's hockey gold was India's 21st gold medal of the Games and sealed the country's fourth-place finish.Golf produced another landmark moment for India.Pranavi Urs won the women's individual gold medal, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games gold in golf.India also won silver in the women's team event through Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar.Olympic medallist Mirabai Chanu claimed silver in the women's 49kg weightlifting event.It was her first Asian Games medal and ended India's wait for a medal in the sport since the 1998 Bangkok Games.Wushu athlete Roshibina Devi also continued her impressive continental run by winning her third consecutive Asian Games medal, taking silver in the women's 60kg sanda event.India's squash contingent also delivered multiple podium finishes.Abhay Singh and Anahat Singh won silver in the men's and women's singles events respectively.Anahat's silver made her the first Indian woman to win a singles silver medal in squash at the Asian Games.India also won bronze medals in mixed doubles and the men's and women's team events.The Aichi-Nagoya campaign was notable not just for the medal count but also for the number of historic achievements.Kumkum Mohod became the first Indian woman to win individual recurve gold at the Asian Games. Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games golf gold.Suchika Tariyal secured India's first Asian Games medal in mixed martial arts, while Jay Meena became the country's first Asian Games medallist in soft tennis after reaching the men's singles semifinals.India also ended long medal droughts in several athletics disciplines.India's success in Aichi-Nagoya also carried significance for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.India secured Olympic quotas through its performances in archery and hockey. The Asian Games offered Olympic qualification opportunities in seven sports — archery, hockey, sailing, squash, surfing, tennis and triathlon.India secured places in both men's and women's hockey as well as in archery's compound mixed team and women's individual recurve events.India's 85-medal haul was 21 medals fewer than its record 106 at Hangzhou, while the gold-medal count dropped from 28 to 21.However, the final standings did not tell the entire story of India's campaign.As recently as Thursday, India had only 10 gold medals and was outside the top 10 of the medal table. A remarkable late surge changed the complexion of the campaign.India won 12 medals on Friday, including six golds, before adding nine medals on the penultimate day. Gold medals in cricket and hockey, along with individual triumphs in wrestling, archery and golf, propelled India into the top five.The final tally of 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals ensured another top-five Asian Games finish and capped a campaign defined by historic firsts, successful title defences and a powerful finish.India may have fallen short of the Hangzhou record, but Aichi-Nagoya 2026 will be remembered as another landmark Asian Games campaign for Indian sport.
Article Summary: India won 85 medals at Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze. The 85-medal haul was India's second-highest ever at the Asian Games, behind the record 106 medals won at Hangzhou 2023. India's medal haul was marked by a late surge, several historic firsts and dominant performances in sports such as athletics, shooting, archery and boxing.

World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka suffered a shock third-round exit at the China Open on Sunday, losing 6-4, 6-3 to Czech Republic’s Nikola Bartunkova. The 34th-ranked Bartunkova produced one of the biggest upsets of the tournament, defeating the four-time Grand Slam champion in one hour and 34 minutes. The Czech hit four aces and capitalised on Sabalenka’s struggles to close out a straight-sets victory.Sabalenka had five break-point opportunities in the opening set but was unable to convert any of them. The Belarusian has never progressed beyond the quarterfinals at the China Open.Sabalenka arrived in Beijing looking to bounce back from her US Open disappointment, where she was denied a third consecutive title by Elena Rybakina. However, Rybakina herself suffered a surprise defeat earlier in Beijing, losing to unseeded Alina Charaeva in the second round.The early exits of the top two seeds mean neither Rybakina nor Sabalenka will feature in the latter stages of the WTA 1000 tournament. The China Open is being played on hard courts in Beijing from September 30 to October 11. Bartunkova will next face Austria’s Sinja Kraus, who defeated Ukraine’s Dayana Yastremska 6-1, 6-4.The Czech will now have an opportunity to extend her breakthrough run in Beijing after taking down one of the tournament’s biggest names.In the men’s draw, top seed Alexander Zverev is scheduled to face Novak Djokovic in the quarterfinals. The Lakers overhauled their roster this summer, and one starting spot still looks unfinished. Walker Kessler and Quentin Grimes arrived, while LeBron James, Marcus Smart and Deandre Ayton left. Lakers need perimeter defense, secondary rim protection and enough offense to hold up. No one on the roster fits it as a proven power forward, and that probably doesn't change before opening night.Derrick Jones Jr. keeps coming up as the fix. The 6-foot-6 Clippers forward, 29, played one season beside Luka Doncic in Dallas, and a Clippers roster stripped of five first-round picks might listen. Reports published October 3 put him forward as an option. Nothing is agreed, and every idea here is speculation, not word from either front office.Los Angeles has two in-house candidates in newcomers Ziaire Williams and Sandro Mamukelashvili, and either could claim the starting power forward job. Right now, it is fair to say that the newcomer duo is a backup option or a trade asset. Jones would upgrade any in-house option as a proven, veteran two-way contributor. His strength, agility and verticality suit a defender beside Doncic, who can feed him enough quality shots to stay viable on offense.As the summer roster changes happened, it looks like the Lakers are reaching the end of perfecting their team. Still, there are some gaps. "The Lakers need a forward and the Los Angeles Clippers need some draft capital, which makes these two teams the perfect trading partners," Fansided’s Mat Issa wrote. "This one would be another reunion for Dončić from his Finals run with the Dallas Mavericks. Here, the Lakers would trade LaRavia, Dalton Knecht and three second-round picks to get Derrick Jones Jr. "Jones is in the final year of his contract and is not expected to get an extension. The league docked the Clippers five first-round picks, and the forward is believed to be among the veterans on their trade block. Moving him before the deadline would return something, while waiting risks losing him for nothing. Los Angeles could also hang back and wait for Jones to test free agency next summer. Washington in Dallas and Herbert Jones in New Orleans are other names on the radar, and Washington looks like the surer option.Doncic, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler and Quentin Grimes already project as four starters, with one spot open. The clock runs in two directions. Los Angeles will judge Williams and Mamukelashvili over roughly two months, and the Clippers face the trade deadline with an expiring contract. If neither Laker claims the spot, the calls start. If the Clippers sit still, Jones may walk next summer with no return. For now, the Lakers have a name, a paper package and no deal.

Seema Kumari: Ended a 16-year Indian medal drought in the women's 10,000m.

Vithya Ramraj: Broke a 42-year-old national record in the women's 400m hurdles while winning bronze.

The gold rush was not simply a repeat

India Found 13 New Golds

NEW DELHI: India won 28 gold medals at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. Four years later, the question in Aichi-Nagoya was how many of those titles it could retain. The answer? - Eight, out of the 28 Hangzhou golds. That’s 28.6 per cent of the total. Twenty titles changed hands.The biggest changes came in the sports that had driven India's record campaign in Hangzhou. All seven shooting golds were lost, while all six athletics titles changed hands and, India also failed to retain either of its two individual compound archery golds.But just the gold-medal count does not tell the whole story. India retained the three compound team archery titles, both kabaddi golds, both cricket titles and the men's hockey crown.The other golds came from a different mix of events and athletes. Some had won silver or bronze in Hangzhou and moved up to gold in Japan. Others won titles in events where India had not been on the podium four years earlier.So while 20 of India's 28 Hangzhou champions failed to retain their titles, the gold medals themselves were replaced from a much wider pool. The Aichi-Nagoya campaign, in that sense, was less about defending the Hangzhou haul and more about how India's medal map had changed in four years.While Shooting had produced seven golds and 22 medals for India at Hangzhou, In Aichi-Nagoya, the overall medal tally fell to 15. The gold count dropped from seven to three, while silver moved from nine to eight and bronze from six to four. The biggest change was that none of India's seven Hangzhou golds was defended in the same event.Instead, India found gold elsewhere. Neeru Dhanda won the women's trap individual title and then partnered Kynan Chenai to win mixed trap. Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh added the mixed 10m air pistol gold.The rifle teams that had delivered two of India's Hangzhou golds - men's 10m air rifle and men's 50m rifle 3 Positions - returned with silver in Japan. There was also a new medal in mixed skeet. Anantjeet Singh Naruka and Parinaaz Dhaliwal won bronze, giving India its first Asian Games medal in the event.So while India's shooting haul was smaller in Aichi-Nagoya, the change was not just in the numbers. The seven golds from Hangzhou were gone, and the three titles in Japan came from a different set of events.While India won 29 athletics medals in Hangzhou, Four years later, the tally in Aichi-Nagoya was 24. The bigger change, though, came in the gold count.Six golds in Hangzhou became one in Japan and that lone title came in the women's 4x400m relay, four years after India's men's relay team had won gold in Hangzhou. Silver medals fell from 14 to nine, while bronze medals increased from nine to 14.There was still plenty of continuity among India's medallists. Murali Sreeshankar again won silver in the long jump. Tajinderpal Singh Toor, the Hangzhou gold medallist, finished with silver this time. Tejaswin Shankar moved from silver to bronze in the decathlon, while Ancy Sojan retained her long-jump silver.Vithya Ramraj again won bronze in the 400m hurdles. Gulveer Singh improved on his Hangzhou performance in the 10,000m, moving from bronze to silver. He also added silver in the 1500m and bronze in the 5000m.So the athletics podium did not disappear in Aichi-Nagoya. India still won 23 medals outside gold. The difference was that performances that had produced six titles in Hangzhou produced only one gold four years later.India matched its Hangzhou tally in archery, winning nine medals again - five gold, two silver and two bronze. The medal distribution, however, changed considerably.The three compound team golds were retained and beyond those events, India had a different set of medal-winning performances in Aichi-Nagoya, particularly in the women's recurve events.Kumkum Mohod won individual recurve gold, while the women's recurve team moved from bronze in Hangzhou to gold in Japan. That left the overall numbers unchanged, but the events behind those numbers were different.The individual compound events also saw a change. India had won medals in both the men's and women's individual compound events in Hangzhou. In Aichi-Nagoya, the men's individual compound event was the notable gap.Boxing went in the opposite direction to shooting and athletics. India had returned from Hangzhou with four medals - one silver and three bronze - but no gold, but In Aichi-Nagoya, the haul rose to six, including three gold medals.Lovlina Borgohain upgraded her silver in the women's 75kg category in 2023, to gold four years later, while Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal added two more titles in categories where India had not won gold at Hangzhou. The bronze tally remained unchanged at three.Wrestling also finished with six medals, the same tally as Hangzhou. But the distribution changed completely. India had won one silver and five bronze medals in 2022, without a gold. In Aichi-Nagoya, that became two golds, two silvers and two bronze medals.Aman Sehrawat and Sujeet Kalkal supplied the two freestyle golds, while Nitesh, added a historic silver in Greco-Roman, and Antim Panghal upgraded her bronze from the 2022 Games to silver in 2026.The bronze tally fell from five to two (Sunil Kumar and Deepak Punia), but India added two golds and one silver.Squash finished with five medals in both Hangzhou and Aichi-Nagoya. But the two golds from 2022 were gone.India's tally changed from two gold, one silver and two bronze to two silver and three bronze. Abhay Singh retained the men's singles silver, replacing Saurav Ghosal on the podium. Anahat Singh added a women's singles medal.The men's team and mixed doubles titles from Hangzhou slipped to bronze in Japan. The women's team retained its bronze, while the mixed-team bronze was not repeated. The overall medal count stayed at five. The two golds did not.India had won all four golds available across the two sports in Hangzhou - the men's and women's cricket titles and the men's and women's kabaddi titles and it repeated that sweep in Japan.In the kabaddi double, both Indian teams came through against Iran in the finals, with the women winning 37-34 and the men 40-34. For the women's team, the victory extended an impressive Asian Games record. India has now won the women's kabaddi gold at every edition it has entered except the 2018 Jakarta Games, when Iran took the title and India settled for silver. The 2026 victory was therefore its fourth gold in five appearances.The men's side has an even longer record. India's 40-34 win over Iran was its ninth Asian Games gold in the men's event across 10 editions. The only time it failed to win the title was in 2018, when Iran took gold. India had returned to the top at Hangzhou and retained the crown in Nagoya.Cricket followed with its own repeat. India's women's team opened the 2026 Games by defending the title it had won at Hangzhou, beating Sri Lanka in the final. The men's team then completed the cricket double on October 3, beating Pakistan to retain the men's gold as well.Hockey produced two very different stories in Aichi-Nagoya. The men's gold was defended. The women's bronze became gold.For the men's team, the 2026 title was significant beyond the medal itself. India beat Malaysia 5-1 in the final to retain the Asian Games crown for the first time, becoming only the second country after Pakistan to win consecutive men's hockey golds. The victory also secured direct qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.The women's title was a different story altogether. India had finished with bronze in Hangzhou. In Japan, it beat defending champions China 1-0 to win the Asian Games gold for the first time since 1982. The victory ended a 44-year wait for gold and also secured direct qualification for LA 2028.It also produced a first for Indian hockey at the Asian Games. For the first time, both the men's and women's teams won gold at the same edition.At Hangzhou, Aditi Ashok won silver, giving India its first women's golf medal at the Asian Games. Four years later, Pranavi Urs went one better.She won individual gold, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games golf title. Urs then joined Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar to win India's first women's team medal in the sport. India's overall golf haul doubled from one medal in Hangzhou to two in Aichi-Nagoya.The individual gold also ended a 24-year wait for India. Shiv Kapur had won the men's title in 2002; Pranavi became the first Indian golfer since then to win an individual Asian Games gold.Sailing: Three medals again, but different eventsSailing produced the same number of medals in both editions. India won three medals in Hangzhou and three again in Aichi-Nagoya. But the events behind those medals changed.Two new skiff events produced podium finishes in Japan, replacing the men's windsurfer and men's dinghy medals from Hangzhou. The women's dinghy medal also changed colour, from silver to bronze.Badminton saw one of India's biggest drops between Hangzhou and Aichi-Nagoya. The medal tally fell from three to one. India's 2022 haul included Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty's men's doubles gold, the men's team silver and HS Prannoy's singles bronze.Four years later, the men's team remained India's only podium finisher. But even that medal changed colour, with the silver becoming bronze.Neither of the two individual medals from Hangzhou was defended. There was no individual podium finish in Aichi-Nagoya, leaving India with just one medal from a sport that had produced three in the previous edition.Rowing's fall was even more pronounced. Five medals in Hangzhou became one bronze in Aichi-Nagoya. In 2022, India had taken two silver and three bronze medals across five events. In Japan, only Satnam Singh and Salman Khan's men's double sculls reached the podium.None of the five events that had delivered medals at Hangzhou did so again. And the build-up itself was unsettled, with last-minute changes to crew combinations and event entries. Arvind Singh, a 2022 silver medallist in the lightweight double sculls, was moved into the quadruple sculls, while Balraj Panwar shifted from the quadruple to the single sculls.Tennis went from two medals in Hangzhou to none in Aichi-Nagoya. The bigger change was the end of India's 36-year medal streak at the Asian Games.India had continued to find tennis medals across different generations, from Leander Paes and Mahesh Bhupathi to Sania Mirza, Rohan Bopanna and the current doubles players. That run ended in Japan.India had three quarterfinal opportunities but could not convert any of them into a medal. Sumit Nagal went out in the singles quarterfinals, while India did not have a women's singles entry. The result was India's first medal-less Asian Games tennis campaign since 1986.Equestrian went from two medals in Hangzhou to none in Aichi-Nagoya. India had won one gold and one bronze in 2022. There was no podium finish this time.The campaign was also affected by selection disputes, the absence of an approved show-jumping team and a setback in eventing. The result was a complete reversal from Hangzhou, with a two-medal haul turning into none in Japan.Aichi-Nagoya also added two new sports to India's Asian Games medal list. Suchika Tariyal won bronze in the women's traditional MMA 60kg category, giving India its first Asian Games medal in mixed martial arts.Jay Meena added another first in soft tennis, winning bronze in men's singles. For Meena, the medal came after two previous Asian Games appearances without a podium finish. He had competed at the 2018 and 2022 Games but returned without a medal on both occasions. In Nagoya, he finally reached the podium.Neither medal replaced a gold lost from Hangzhou. They came from sports that had not previously contributed an Asian Games medal to India.Weightlifting produced another long-gap story. Mirabai Chanu's silver in the women's 49kg category was India's first Asian Games weightlifting medal since Karnam Malleswari's silver at Bangkok 1998.There was also a personal milestone. Chanu had Olympic and World Championship medals and Commonwealth Games titles, but an Asian Games medal had remained missing. The silver in Nagoya completed the collection.India had not won a kurash medal at the previous Asian Games. Pincky Balhara put the sport back on India's medal list in Aichi-Nagoya, winning bronze in the women's -78kg category. It was a return to the podium rather than a title defence, adding another sport to India's 2026 medal tally.Wushu, Table Tennis, sepak takraw: Medals from the wider fieldWushu again produced a medal through Roshibina Devi, who won silver in the women's 60kg sanda - her third Asian Games medal.Table tennis added bronze through Diya Chitale and Manush Shah in mixed doubles, while World No.3 men’s pair of Manush Shah and Manav Thakar flattered to deceive.India also retained its bronze in sepak takraw, with the men's quadrant team finishing on the podium again.The other side: Four sports drop out of India's medal listThe Hangzhou-to-Aichi-Nagoya comparison also has a different side. Some sports that had contributed medals in 2022 did not produce one in Japan.Chess, bridge, roller sports and canoeing had together contributed six medals to India's Hangzhou tally - two silver in chess, one silver in bridge, two bronze in roller sports and one bronze in canoeing. None of those four sports were part of the Aichi-Nagoya programme.The changing medal map also showed up in the number of firsts India recorded in Aichi-Nagoya.Thirteen of India's 2026 gold medals came from events in which India had either won silver or bronze at Hangzhou, or had not won a medal at all. That included three shooting golds.The mixed 10m air pistol moved from silver to gold, while Neeru Dhanda won the women's individual trap and mixed trap titles in events where India had not won gold in Hangzhou.Athletics produced another upgrade, with the women's 4x400m relay moving from silver to gold.Archery's women's recurve team went from bronze to gold, while Kumkum Mohod added the individual recurve title.Boxing produced three more. Lovlina Borgohain moved from silver to gold in the women's 75kg category. Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal won titles in categories where India had not taken gold in Hangzhou.Wrestling followed the same pattern. Sujeet Kalkal won the men's 65kg title, while Aman Sehrawat moved from bronze in 2022 to gold in the 57kg category.In golf, Pranavi Urs turned Aditi Ashok's women's individual silver from Hangzhou into gold. Women's hockey completed another major upgrade, moving from bronze in Hangzhou to gold in Aichi-Nagoya.Taken together, these 13 golds explain why the 2026 campaign cannot be judged simply by counting how many Hangzhou champions retained their titles.India did lose 20 of its 28 Hangzhou golds, but several of those losses were replaced by athletes who had finished lower on the podium in 2022, or had not reached it at all.The fact that India defended only eight of its 28 Hangzhou golds does not mean the 2026 campaign simply replaced the previous one with a broader or better model. Hangzhou had a heavy concentration of gold at the top. Shooting won seven. Athletics won six. Archery won five. Together, those three disciplines accounted for 18 of India's 28 gold medals in 2022. That made Hangzhou's medal profile very different from Aichi-Nagoya.And the disciplines that lost the most golds in Japan did not disappear from the podium. Shooting remained one of India's biggest medal contributors with 15 medals. Athletics produced 24, while archery matched its Hangzhou total of nine. So the change was not that India's traditional strengths stopped producing medals. They simply produced fewer golds.
Article Summary: India won 28 gold medals at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. Twenty per cent of the total gold medals changed hands. India's record was broken with seven golds in shooting. All six athletics titles changed hands, while all six cricket titles also failed to retain.
