Article Title: Asian Games hockey official Gurinder Sangha leaves Japan amid sexual misconduct complaints
Article Text:
India's women's hockey team at Asian Games

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kolkata: Gurinder Singh Sangha, a Jalandhar-based international hockey umpire and technical official who was appointed by the Asian Hockey Federation (AHF) as umpire manager for the hockey competition at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, has left Japan before the tournament concluded following multiple complaints of alleged sexual misconduct against him.Sources alleged that Sangha misbehaved with a female hockey official from Malaysia.“A Malaysian official has complained that he tried to hug and kiss her in the name of mentoring, and he has had to leave the Asian Games in Nagoya midway, Hockey India leadership is having conversations about starting an investigation,” said a Hockey India official.The HI official said the latest allegations had once again raised questions about Sangha's conduct and the handling of earlier complaints against him.Meanwhile, Asima Ali, Hockey India vice-president and executive member, welcomed the development.“There can be no tolerance for any form of sexual misconduct in sport. The message has to be clear that complaints will be taken seriously and acted upon promptly. We must be stern in our dealing with such offenders and ensure that the sport remains a safe environment for everyone,” said Ali.Multiple sources also alleged that Sangha, who has previously officiated at major events, including the Asian Games, Olympic qualifiers and the Asia Cup, behaved inappropriately with a member of the hotel staff and showed her obscene videos in his room.The latest complaint is not the first allegation levelled against Sangha. During the Hockey India League in Ranchi in January 2025, a female umpire filed a formal complaint against him while he was serving as Umpires' Manager. Hockey India subsequently confirmed receipt of the complaint and constituted a three-member committee to conduct a preliminary investigation into the matter.According to the complaint, the umpire alleged that Sangha's conduct during an interaction at the team hotel in Ranchi on January 20, 2025, was "unwanted and inappropriate" and left her uncomfortable.In a communication dated Jan 21, 2025, Bhola Nath Singh, secretary general of Hockey India, informed stakeholders that a three-member panel had been constituted in consultation with the federation's Internal Complaint Committee for Prevention of Sexual Harassment to carry out a preliminary investigation and submit its report within two days.The latest episode comes amid increased scrutiny of misconduct complaints within Indian hockey. Earlier this year, Hockey India removed a support staff member from a national camp after harassment allegations surfaced against him, stating that action had been taken immediately after the matter came to its notice.The federation has also grappled with other complaints in recent times, including an April 2026 complaint alleging sexual harassment and abuse of authority by a Hockey India official, and a 2025 case involving misconduct allegations against a junior women's team coach.During the inaugural Women's Hockey India League, a coach was also removed overnight after authorities were informed of harassment complaints involving younger players.
Article Summary: Gurinder Singh Sangha has been accused of sexual misconduct. Sangha was appointed by the Asian Hockey Federation as umpire manager for the hockey competition at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya. Sources alleged that Sangha misbehaved with a female hockey official from Malaysia.

Article Title: Parveen Hooda holds her nerve to clinch Asian Games boxing gold in 3-2 thriller
Article Text:
India's Parveen Hooda (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lovlina ends India's 12-year wait

Parveen Hooda completed a remarkable comeback by clinching the women's 65kg boxing gold at the Asian Games , beating Chinese Taipei's Chen Nien-Chen 3-2 in a split decision in a closely fought final.The Indian boxer had to dig deep in the deciding round after Chen levelled the contest following two rounds. Parveen held her nerve in a tense finish, relying on her counter-punching as the Chinese Taipei boxer pressed for the decisive blows.The victory adds another boxing gold for India on a day when Lovlina Borgohain also stood atop the podium.Parveen made a cautious start to the final, with both boxers initially keeping their distance. She found success with her counters before stepping in with combinations, including some effective body shots. The judges awarded her the opening round 5-0.Chen responded in the second round. Parveen continued to use her reach and movement to keep her opponent at bay, but Chen found her range with quick 1-2 combinations and landed enough clean punches to take the round 10-9 on all five cards.With the scores level heading into the final round, Chen came out aggressively and landed a couple of early jabs.Parveen weathered the pressure and began finding openings with quick combinations of her own.The Indian then switched to counter-punching as Chen pushed forward in the closing stages. The strategy proved enough to edge the contest, with Parveen winning the final by a 3-2 split decision.The gold marks a significant turnaround for Parveen, whose medal from the Hangzhou Asian Games was revoked following a doping violation. She had also exited the 2026 Commonwealth Games at the quarterfinal stage.Chen, a former world champion, came into the final as the 2026 Asian Championships gold medallist and had also won bronze at the previous Asian Games and the Paris Olympics.Earlier on Friday, Lovlina Borgohain ended India's 12-year wait for an Asian Games women's boxing gold by defeating China's Ziyi Bao in the women's 75kg final.The Olympic bronze medallist secured a 5-0 unanimous decision to upgrade the silver medal she won at the previous edition, giving herself a gold medal on her birthday.Lovlina became only the second Indian woman after MC Mary Kom to win an Asian Games boxing gold. Mary Kom had claimed the 51kg title at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain ends India's 12-year wait for an Asian Games women's boxing gold by defeating China's Ziyi Bao in the women's 75kg final. Parveen Hooda completed a remarkable comeback by clinching the women’s 65kg boxing gold at the Asian Games.

MUMBAI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park on Friday, questioning his repeated references to his past as a tea seller.In a video posted by news agency IANS, Dipke said, "This person is just travelling around the world with our money. One thing is that he keeps saying, 'I have sold tea, I have sold tea, I have sold tea.' Why did you sell tea? Did we ask you to sell tea? We said you could have gone to school, studied, and got a job."Dipke also quipped, "PM Modi's fashion sense and skin care is on point. Even the big actors, models cannot match his style."The CJP founder was addressing thousands of people who gathered at Shivaji Park despite Mumbai Police denying permission for the protest.The demonstration was held to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Dipke also accused Delhi Police Deputy Commissioner of Police Sachin Sharma of being close to Union home minister Amit Shah while referring to the police action during the separate Delhi protest."Some police officers were telling me that this Sachin Sharma is a Sanghi. He is Amit Shah’s favourite. So I want to tell Sachin Sharma: if you are a Sanghi, wear khaki shorts (RSS uniform), don’t wear the police uniform!" he said.Dipke also said the turnout at Shivaji Park would overwhelm the barricades put up by the authorities."So many people will arrive that your barricades won’t be enough!" Dipke said.The CJP has demanded Kumar's resignation, criminal proceedings against him, a freeze on the SIR exercise and restoration of the January 2025 voter list.The protests followed a report in The Indian Express that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on at least 14 occasions over a 10-month period on matters involving electoral rolls, voter registration and the Commission's technology systems.The Election Commission has rejected suggestions of an internal rift and maintained that decisions taken by the poll panel, including those relating to SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of all three commissioners.CJP spokesperson Saurav Das had earlier urged Mumbaikars to join the protest and accused Kumar of being a "traitor" and the "real anti-national"."The youth of the whole country, the young generation, everyone came out last time for the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan. And this time too, it is going to be the same with Gyanesh Kumar, who is a traitor to the country. The youth of Mumbai are hitting the streets again. Today, a massive protest is going to happen at Shivaji Park. And I want, I appeal to all the Mumbaikars and our friends. Everyone come," Das said.Veteran actor Shabana Azmi and singer Vishal Dadlani were among those who addressed the gathering, while actor Naseeruddin Shah and other public figures also joined the protest.Azmi said the demonstration was about democracy, people's rights and the right to vote."This is a question of our democracy. It is a question of our rights. It is a question of our voice. We have been told since childhood to cast our votes, claim our rights, and raise our voices. But when our fundamental right is snatched away or manipulated, what is a person supposed to do?""Naturally, they will protest, and this "people's power" is unstoppable now. Once the spark is lit, you can see how it spreads; it is happening all across India...The names of thousands upon thousands of people have been removed from the lists...After today's protest, we will see if action is taken or if we have to keep fighting this battle. We have to fight the battle for as long as it takes," Azmi said.Dadlani said the issue should concern supporters of all political parties if the election system was compromised."I would say this is extremely important. You may support any political party, but if the country's election system itself is compromised, then the country and democracy will no longer survive.""So, I would tell everyone, even those who support the BJP, that they too are with us and are part of this country. So I would tell them as well: wake up. Remove Gyanesh Kumar, reverse this entire process, eliminate the SIR, and protect every citizen's right to vote," Dadlani said.The CJP demonstration was also met by a counter-protest by a group identifying itself as "Gen Next Mumbai".One counter-protester accused Dipke and others of speaking about dismantling the Constitution and said the group had gathered to defend it."People like Abhijeet Dipke speak of dismantling the Constitution. Today, however, we stand beneath the statue of Babasaheb Ambedkar because we know how to protect and respect the Constitution. That is why we have gathered here for a peaceful demonstration; the conduct of the Cockroach Janata Party will not be tolerated," the protester said.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis also hit back at the protesters, saying allegations against the Election Commission had already been countered."The entire matter has been exposed. Following the press conference held by the three Election Commissioners, their fake narrative has been busted. Yet, attempts are still being made to push this fake narrative. They will not succeed in this," Fadnavis said.In Delhi, opposition leaders and youth organisations staged a demonstration near Jantar Mantar against the Election Commission and demanded Kumar's removal. Police had denied permission for the protest and imposed restrictions under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal accused the government and the Election Commission of undermining people's voting rights and said opposition leaders were prepared to face arrest."This is for saving the democracy of the country, saving the vote for a common man. Common men's votes are snatched by Modi and Shah through the Election Commission of India. So, this is a do-or-die fight for the Congress party and the INDIA alliance and all other opposition parties. We are not going to allow this thing," Venugopal said.Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also backed the protests, saying thousands of young people were exercising their constitutional rights and demanding Kumar's resignation."Today is Gandhi Jayanti. And today, thousands of young people are on the streets against vote theft - peacefully, without violence, exercising their constitutional rights. Their demand is clear: Gyanesh Kumar must resign. Save democracy," Gandhi said in a post on X.BJP spokesperson Ajay Alok said protests were legitimate but protesters had to follow prescribed rules and obtain permission."In any democratic system, holding protests is absolutely legitimate, but there are certain rules and procedures to follow. Permission must be obtained, and people can protest wherever they want within the prescribed rules. Our country is democratic, so anyone can protest. However, if the rules are not followed, people may be detained. Detention during protests is, in any case, a common occurrence," Alok said.The protests come amid an ongoing political dispute over the Election Commission's handling of SIR and allegations concerning electoral rolls. The Election Commission has maintained that its decisions on SIR were taken unanimously.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questions PM Modi's past as a tea seller. Demonstration held to demand resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. CJP has demanded Kumar's resignation, criminal proceedings against him, a freeze on the SIR exercise.

Article Title: Woman convicted of killing 10-year-old held in Delhi after 20 years in hiding
Article Text:
She changed her name to Pooja and moved through different places to avoid detection. (AI Image)





NEW DELHI: For more than 20 years, Sadhana managed to live away from prison where she was to serve a life sentence. A life convict in a kidnapping-murder case of a 10-year-old boy, Sadhana went missing after walking out on parole in Dec 2005.Over the years, police said, she changed her name, moved cities and built a new life as Pooja. Last week, Delhi Police ’s crime branch arrested her in Haridwar.The case dates back to Jan 6, 1990, when the boy went missing from Azadpur T-point. Police said witnesses Jagdish Chand and Vasdev had seen Sadhana holding his hand while crossing GT Road around 5.30pm. Sadhana and co-accused Raj Kumar were arrested from Jahangirpuri.The two were living together and the child’s father, Balwant Ram, and his family had objected to it. A previous dispute led to resentment and a decision to take revenge, police said.During the trial, Sadhana was found to be the last person seen with the child. Police said she had also concealed Kumar’s presence at her house and played an active role in the conspiracy. She was convicted under sections 302 (murder), 364 (kidnapping or abducting in order to murder) and 120B (criminal conspiracy) of IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment.Sadhana was lodged in Tihar Jail on Jan 9, 1990.After spending years in jail, Sadhana was released on parole on Dec 27, 2005, which was extended by three weeks on medical grounds. She, however, did not surrender on Jan 18, 2006, and began a second life.She changed her name to Pooja and moved through different places to avoid detection. Police said her final parole was arranged by another Raj Kumar, a Tilak Nagar resident, on the reference of Janki, a woman who was lodged with Sadhana in jail. Sadhana stayed with him before taking up a job at a private company in Noida.There, she met Keshav, a carpenter. They moved to Mukundpur, where they lived for around five years before shifting to Haridwar. Police said Sadhana married Keshav in a temple and used his name as her husband in documents, helping conceal her identity.Meanwhile, investigators continued to pursue leads through intelligence, old associates and family links. A recent lead about a woman living under an assumed identity took a team to Haridwar and Sadhana was arrested on Sept 27. Her years of borrowed independence came to an end as she was sent back to jail.
Article Summary: Sadhana went missing after walking out on parole in Dec 2005. Over the years, police said, she changed her name, moved cities and built a new life as Pooja. Last week, Delhi Police ’s crime branch arrested her in Haridwar. The case dates back to Jan 6, 1990, when the boy went missing from Azadpur T-point.

India’s medal-winning campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 has reached 80 medals, with the contingent winning 18 gold, 26 silver and 36 bronze medals. India are currently fifth in the overall medal standings.India’s medal tally received a major boost over the last two days, with the contingent adding gold medals across boxing, wrestling, archery, hockey and golf. Lovlina Borgohain, Parveen Hooda, Ankush Panghal, Sujeet Kalkal, the Indian women’s hockey team, Kumkum Mohod and Pranavi Urs have all contributed gold medals to India’s latest surge.Kumkum also won silver alongside Dhiraj Bommadevara in the mixed recurve team event, while India’s women’s golf team of Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar secured silver.On October 3, Kumkum Mohod added another gold by winning the women’s individual recurve event. The 17-year-old defeated South Korea’s Oh Yejin 6-5 in a shoot-off to become the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve medal at the Asian Games. Her victory also secured an Olympic quota place for India for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.Pranavi Urs also scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman to win individual golf gold at the Asian Games, while helping India claim silver in the women’s team event alongside Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar.India’s women’s cricket team won the country’s first gold medal of the Games after defeating Sri Lanka in the final. Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet then added India’s second gold by winning the 10m air pistol mixed team event.India subsequently won both the men’s and women’s kabaddi titles, while Neeru Dhanda secured gold in the women’s trap event. She later teamed up with Kynan Chenai to win the mixed trap team gold.In athletics, Kiran Pahal, Poovamma Machettira, Prachi Choudhary and Vithya Ramraj won gold in the women’s 4x400m relay. India also dominated the compound archery events, winning gold in the men’s team, women’s team and mixed team events.On October 2, Lovlina Borgohain defeated China’s Bao Ziyi 5-0 in the women’s 75kg final to win gold. The victory came on her birthday and made Lovlina only the second Indian woman boxer after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games gold.The women’s recurve team of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod then created history by defeating South Korea 5-3 to win India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the event.India then added three more gold medals in boxing and wrestling, with Parveen Hooda winning the women’s 65kg title, Ankush Panghal taking gold in the men’s 80kg category and Sujeet Kalkal winning the men’s freestyle 65kg event.The Indian women’s hockey team ended a 44-year wait for Asian Games gold by defeating China 1-0 in the final, with the victory also securing a direct qualification spot for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.On October 3, Kumkum completed a memorable Asian Games campaign by winning individual recurve gold. After being pushed to a shoot-off by Oh Yejin, the 17-year-old held her nerve to shoot a 10 and beat the South Korean 8, securing India’s first individual women’s recurve gold at the Asian Games.Pranavi Urs added another historic gold in golf. The 23-year-old became the first Indian woman to win an individual golf gold medal at the Asian Games. She also helped India win silver in the women’s team event.India’s silver medal haul has come across shooting, athletics, weightlifting, wushu, squash, wrestling, sailing, archery and golf.The shooting contingent has been one of India’s biggest contributors, with medals across air rifle, 50m rifle 3 positions, 25m pistol and trap events.Mirabai Chanu ended her long wait for an Asian Games medal by taking silver in the women’s 49kg weightlifting event, while Roshibina Devi won silver in women’s 60kg sanda. Gulveer Singh also enjoyed a strong Games, winning silver in the men’s 10,000m and 1500m events.In squash, Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh won silver in the women’s and men’s singles events respectively. India also collected silver medals in sailing and archery, with Prince Noble Kurisinkal and Manu Francis finishing second in the men’s skiff.Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara lost to China in the mixed recurve final, while Dhiraj Bommadevara, Neeraj Chauhan and Yashdeep Bhoge finished runners-up to South Korea in the men’s recurve team event.The latest addition came in golf, where Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar won silver in the women’s team event. China took gold, while India finished second.India’s bronze medals have come from a wide range of disciplines, including shooting, athletics, squash, boxing, wrestling, archery, sailing, sepaktakraw, badminton, rowing, table tennis, kurash, soft tennis and mixed martial arts.Athletics has produced a large share of India’s bronze medals, with Parul Chaudhary, Gulveer Singh, Tejaswin Shankar, Vithya Ramraj, Pooja Singh, Rohit Yadav and others contributing to the tally.India’s squash contingent has also produced multiple medals, with Joshna Chinappa, Velavan Senthilkumar, Anahat Singh, Tanvi Khanna, Abhay Singh and Veer Chotrani contributing across the mixed doubles and team events.In boxing, Narender Berwal, Priya Ghanghas and Kapil Pokhariya won bronze, while Sunil Kumar secured bronze in Greco-Roman wrestling.Nethra Kumanan won bronze in the women’s dinghy sailing event, while India’s men’s quadrant team secured bronze in sepaktakraw after losing 0-2 to Japan in the semifinal.
Article Summary: India's women's hockey team clinch Gold at Asian Games 2026. India's men's kabaddi team won four gold medals. India won two silver medals. The team won two golds and a silver medal in the women's tournament.

Article Title: India-Pakistan cricket, hockey clashes set Asian Games viewership records: OCA
Article Text:
India beat Pakistan by 19 runs in the Asian Games men’s T20 final to claim gold after posting 211/6 and restricting Pakistan to 192. (Image: Reuters)

Challenges behind the Games

India-Pakistan clashes in cricket and hockey became the biggest-viewed matches in Asian Games history, according to the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA). The announcement came as officials highlighted the sporting records and overall athlete experience at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.India defeated Pakistan 4-3 in the men’s hockey semifinal in Kakamigahara before beating Malaysia to win gold. In cricket, India edged Pakistan by 19 runs in the men’s final."The broadcast had the biggest viewership ever for the Games. Thanks to two big matches: yesterday, the Pakistan-India cricket match was the most-viewed match, and the day before (on Thursday), the Pakistan-India hockey match was the most-viewed match ever in the Games’ history," OCA Coordination Committee President Tayyab Ikram said.No viewership figures were disclosed, and officials did not say which of the two matches attracted the larger audience.The Games also faced criticism over accommodation and transport after organisers chose not to build a traditional Athletes' Village. Athletes and officials stayed across hotels, temporary structures and a cruise ship.Ikram acknowledged the difficulties but defended the approach."We are also aware that there were some complaints, and there were certain issues which were highlighted.Of course there were some challenges, but the way we handled the challenges, should be more important to highlight."OCA Director General Husain Al-Musallam said the Games produced 54 world records, 11 junior world records, 89 Asian records and 212 Asian Games records."This achievement does not come without the best environment the organising committee created for the athletes."He added that the OCA’s marketing and sponsorship revenue was 19 per cent higher than at Hangzhou 2023, while officials said future Games could adopt more sustainable and economical hosting models without compromising athletes’ experience.

NEW DELHI: A 36-year-old man has been arrested for allegedly stabbing his wife to death following an argument over his suspected extra-marital affair, police said on Sunday.The accused, identified as Pardeep, who runs a biryani stall, was arrested from Dwarka Sector-20.According to police, a PCR call reporting a stabbing near Kali Mata Mandir in JJ Colony, Palam, was received at 4.49 pm on September 27."The woman, identified as Sonia (30), was rushed to Indira Gandhi Hospital, where doctors declared her brought dead. Article Title: When cow dung was used to create a homegrown astro-turf
Article Text:
Former hockey captain Zafar Iqbal at his residence in Ghaziabad





NEW DELHI: At 70, Zafar Iqbal is still playing to win. Once he finished a floodlight game past midnight and started again at 7am the next day. The septuagenarian's game is, however, no longer hockey.The Olympic gold medal winner is now devoted to golf. Zafar's handicap runs in double digits, but he is winning pro-am events with abandon. "I have shot hole-in-ones on three occasions," he says with glee and relish.But "golf", he adds, "is a tough game. You have to fight against yourself."Zafar, though, has fought tougher battles on the hockey field in a long, storied career. For instance, the desperate, dying minutes against Spain in the 1980 Moscow gold medal game, which he still remembers like it happened yesterday. As against Pakistan last Thursday in the Asian Games , India led 3-0 early in that game.But with five minutes left, the gap narrowed to an agonising 4-3, with Juan Amat, the tall and lethal penalty corner specialist, firing a hat-trick for Spain, also the 1974 European champions."We won, but if the game had continued for a few minutes, anything could have happened. 'Hamaari hawa kharab ho gayi thhi' (We were all at sea, completely overrun)," recalls Zafar.Interestingly, even the 2026 Asian Games semi-final against Pakistan finished with the same scoreline.If Moscow produced the most cherished moment of his career, New Delhi offered the saddest, when India were routed 7-1 by Pakistan in the 1982 Asian Games final. Zafar scored India's lone goal off a penalty stroke."The defence had collapsed. After losing the match, we didn't leave the dressing room till 9pm. At the Games village, we didn't even dare to go to the dining room. Some wrestlers and hospitality people brought food to our rooms. In the space of an hour, we had become zeroes from heroes," he says.Zafar belongs to the generation that played on grass at home and battled astro-turf abroad. The first astro-turf in India was laid out only in 1982, six years after it appeared in the 1976 Montreal Olympics.He talks about an instance of 'jugaad' in Patiala in the when, to provide the artificial feel of astro-turf, the ground was stripped of grass and then plastered with cow dung cake mixed in water. "This was supposed to create a fast-paced pitch and give players a feel of astro-turf," he says.Zafar was born in village Harganwa near the communally sensitive town of Bihar Sharif, but bred in Aligarh Muslim University , where his father, a PhD from Manchester, taught organic chemistry.He grew up in an academic environment in the campus, where family conversations typically focused on which neighbour's child had passed medical or engineering entrance exams.But the university also had a strong sports culture. Zafar loved both studies and sports. He was the captain of his school football team. "But a 'dada' (toughie) in school wanted someone else to be the captain," he recalls.At this point, two gentlemen were critical in shaping his career. One was Zillur Rehman Khan, who taught physics but was passionate about hockey. Impressed by the way Zafar flicked the ball from the top of the D, Zillur not only made Zafar the school's hockey team captain, but also called him to practise with the college players."When my flicks turned out to be better than theirs, he started laughing at them," Zafar remembers.If Zillur was his mentor, Jagan Nath, manager of the 1936 Berlin Olympics team, was his first serious coach. A disciplinarian, he didn't like players wearing sunglasses."He would tell us, 'God gave you eyes to see. Why do you need sunglasses?' But he was also a good coach, who gave you confidence," recalls Zafar.Striking a fine balance between higher studies and hockey was tough. Zafar would wake up when the streetlights were still alive, dribble all the way to the ground, eat gud-chana, then considered a 'special' diet for sportspersons, have a bath, eat breakfast, and leave for civil engineering classes by 7.40am.He would return home for lunch, before leaving for the ground again at 3pm. "I would reach an hour before others to work on fitness and improve the accuracy of my shots," Zafar says. He would come back only at 6pm and sit down to study. "It was a tough schedule," he says.But Zafar dribbled between both. He not only was selected for the combined universities and made his international debut as a 'left-in' against Holland, but also earned his civil engineering degree.When he was selected for the national team, coach Kishan Lal, who captained India in the 1948 London Olympics, called him and said, "Can you play 'left-out'? Another player has to play 'left-in'.""I said, 'Yes sir, I will'. But it wasn't easy. We grew up playing positional hockey. I had to rework my style of play. But I learnt. And I played as a 'left-out' for the rest of my life."In time, Zafar would lead the national team, become coach and selector, and work for Indian Airlines . "After my initial years as a sports officer, I would look after construction and maintenance," he says. He would also receive the Arjuna Award and the Padma Shri.In their second innings, sportspersons often take to golf. Cricketers Kapil Dev and Roger Binny belong to that group. Zafar adds two former hockey internationals - goalie Romeo James and defender MP Singh - to that list.He follows hockey but also watched the Asian Games medal-winning women's golf team on TV. He even cracks jokes on the game's addictive nature. At 70, Zafar Iqbal is clearly savouring life, one putt at a time, on the fairways and greens.
Article Summary: Olympic gold medal winner Zafar Iqbal is now devoted to golf. His handicap runs in double digits, but he is winning pro-am events with abandon. He has fought tougher battles on the hockey field in a long, storied career.

Article Title: Abhijeet Dipke calls CJP an 'accident' that gave hope to millions
Article Text:
Abhijeet Dipke of the Cockroach Janta Party has responded to criticisms by focusing on youth issues

Dipke says CJP will focus on youth issues

October 10 Jantar Mantar protest





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has hit back at what he described as "constant attempts" to discredit the outfit, saying the party would rather focus on the issues facing young people than engage in fights with critics.In a post on X, Dipke said the youth was already frustrated with established political parties and their internal "bickering"."I have a lot to say about the constant attempts by some to discredit CJP, but honestly, there’s no point," Dipke said.He said the younger generation was frustrated with what he described as infighting among established political parties, alleging that political groups were more concerned about their own prominence than the people they claimed to represent."The youth is already frustrated with exactly this kind of bickering among established political parties, where everyone seems more concerned about their own prominence than the people they claim to represent," he said.Dipke described the formation of CJP as an "accident" that eventually gave hope to millions."The formation of CJP was one big accident which ended up giving hope to millions. Fighting for those youth and the issues they face is far more important than wasting our energy fighting with those who have already decided to discredit us, no matter what we do," he said.His remarks came after CJP stepped up its agitation seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The party held a major protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park on Friday, thousands gathered despite police denying permission for the event.After the Mumbai protest, Dipke announced another demonstration at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10 if Gyanesh Kumar does not resign."If Gyanesh Kumar doesn't resign, cockroaches from across India will march to Delhi & protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10," Dipke said in an X post, describing the proposed agitation as peaceful and calling on citizens who want free and fair elections to join.The CJP has been demanding Kumar's resignation and has raised allegations concerning electoral-roll revisions and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). The allegations made by the organisation have not been independently verified.CJP, critics trade barbs amid election-roll protestThe latest remarks also come amid a war of words between CJP and its critics. CJP co-conveners Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das recently hit out at what they called a "self-declared liberal" ecosystem for criticising Dipke and the party.Meanwhile, protests against Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi have also seen hundreds of demonstrators detained as protesters attempted to reach Jantar Mantar.Dipke has now said the party's focus would remain on issues concerning young people rather than on those seeking to discredit it.
Article Summary: Abhijeet Dipke of the Cockroach Janta Party has responded to criticisms by focusing on youth issues. His remarks came after CJP stepped up its agitation seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. CJP co- conveners recently hit out at what they called a "self-declared liberal" ecosystem.

India pacers Mukesh Kumar and Akash Deep shared nine wickets as Rest of India beat reigning Ranji Trophy champions Jammu and Kashmir by 167 runs on the fourth day to win the 2026-27 Irani Cup in Srinagar on Sunday.Mukesh returned figures of 6/33 to claim his 11th five-wicket haul in first-class cricket and dismantle the Jammu and Kashmir batting line-up. Akash, playing his comeback game, supported his Bengal teammate with 3/25 as J&K, chasing 279, were bowled out for 111.The bowling effort completed a win that had been set up by Ravichandran Smaran, who scored 68 in the first innings and 135 in the second. Smaran helped Rest of India recover from difficult positions in both innings as they went on to win despite conceding a 41-run first-innings lead.Jammu and Kashmir needed only to hold on for a draw to lift the trophy because of their first-innings lead. They appeared to be on course for a favourable result after openers Shubham Khajuria and Qamran Iqbal put together 54 runs for the first wicket.Akash broke the partnership by trapping Iqbal lbw in front of the wicket. Mukesh then struck twice just before lunch, dismissing Shubham Pundir and captain Paras Dogra off successive deliveries in the 15th over.Dogra was bowled after the delivery moved away just enough to beat his defence and hit the middle stump.J&K went into lunch at 89/3 after 19 overs, with Khajuria on 36 and Abdul Samad on six.Khajuria was dismissed by Akash with the first ball after lunch, triggering a collapse. J&K lost their next six wickets for just 22 runs over the following nine overs.Mukesh finished with 6/33, while Akash took 3/25. Akash's workload in the match, which included six wickets across 23.3 overs, will please the national management ahead of India's upcoming tour of New Zealand, with the pacer now appearing to have recovered well enough to be considered for selection.Earlier, Rest of India, who resumed their second innings at 306/8, were bowled out for 319. Umar Nazir, Sunil Kumar and Sahil Lotra took three wickets each for J&K.237 and 319278 and 111 all out in 28.4 overs (Shubham Khajuria 36; Mukesh Kumar 6/33, Akash Deep 3/25) by 167 runs.
